summary: Uneven attach latencies & throughput sag from coordinated mini-fanout + sidecar logstorm in dedicated pool
description: Summary: During the 02:00-03:00 UTC window on 2026-03-12 BrightHelp observed sustained p50/p95 latency regressions for their dedicated capacity routes and dramatically reduced throughput. Traffic patterns showed many small concurrent streams (mini-fanout) from the customer's analytics sidecar processes. Simultaneously, our sidecar-metrics process emitted a burst of high-frequency logs and connections to the allocator, correlating with attach latencies and an apparent GPU credit sink. Impact: BrightHelp reported increased timeouts and degraded batch throughput impacting job completion SLAs for their nightly window. Several requests hit internal timeouts and experienced fallbacks to lower-tier models. Environment: prod-us-east dedicated pool (reserved cluster ID: dp-44b2).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate 600 small streams (avg 150ms per message) across 20 clients to a dedicated route pinned to dp-44b2
2) Start a sidecar log emitter (high-frequency heartbeat + debug logs) that opens ephemeral connections every 30-60s
3) Observe attach latencies and allocator attach/release rates for 20 minutes
4) Compare autoscaler decisions during the burst window with baseline traffic profile
logs: 2026-03-12T02:07:14Z ERROR sidecar-metrics connection error: dial tcp 10.1.4.23:443: i/o timeout
2026-03-12T02:09:00Z INFO fallback routing applied to brighthelp/analytics -> redwood/long-context-v1-lite
timeline: 02:00 UTC - BrightHelp scheduled nightly flush; traffic ramps with many small streams
02:04 UTC - Sidecar-metrics spike detected (high connection churn + verbose debug enabled)
02:06 UTC - First attach latency alerts fired (p99 > 1.2s)
02:10 UTC - Autoscaler paused growth after telemetry drop and issued hold decision
02:22 UTC - Partial mitigation: support disabled verbose sidecar logging for customer; attach latencies improved
03:15 UTC - Throughput returned to baseline after sidecar logging stopped and allocators recovered
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: High-rate sidecar log connections were creating ephemeral connection noise that prevented timely allocator handoffs, leading to transient GPU credit depletion.
Hypothesis B: The autoscaler interpreted the telemetry anomalies as reduced efficiency and hesitated to scale, compounding the attach lag.
Preliminary finding: GPU credit counter dropped rapidly during logstorm window; NVLink and PCIe metrics show elevated io_wait coordinating with attach spikes.
Heap: No kernel OOMs or driver crashes were observed. No scheduled cluster maintenance in window.
Related patterns: Similar connection/log storms previously surfaced in SUP-712909 and SUP-271400 but topology here showed stronger correlation to autoscaler hold decisions.
comments: Support (Aisha): Reached out to BrightHelp for immediate mitigation options and requested temporary reduction of sidecar logging level.
SRE (Liam): Collected perf profiles, heap snapshots and GPU credit counters. Raising autoscaler sensitivity for this pool to allow conservative scale-up until telemetry stabilizes.
Customer (BrightHelp - OpS): Confirmed we can flip sidecar debug->info for tonight's window; asked if Redwood can proactively prevent autoscaler hold on noisy telemetry.
Eng (Maya Chen): Proposed patch to add sidecar connection-rate as an input to autoscaler heuristic (PR draft linked).
Support (Aisha): Noting customer appreciative of quick mitigation; will monitor next nightly window and update ticket with metrics.
SRE (Liam) - 2026-03-14: Added temporary rule to ignore short-lived telemetry dips < 30s when computing scale-up decisions for dedicated pools. Monitoring for regressions.
resolution: In Progress - temporary mitigations applied: instructed customer to disable verbose sidecar logging (customer accepted) and adjusted autoscaler sensitivity for dp-44b2 to avoid hold decisions on short telemetry drops. Follow-ups: 1) Implement autoscaler heuristic change (eng PR in progress). 2) Add a runbook entry for sidecar-induced attach noise and safe mitigations. 3) Re-run chaos test to validate behavior. Customer to confirm next nightly job metrics; if stable, schedule permanent autoscaler heuristic rollout.
